A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iNatSounds/XCDC benchmark and AG-CLIP research, despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, equations and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original geolocation experiments on iNatSounds and XCDC, component ablations, spatiotemporal aggregation results and multimodal case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds WABAD evaluation, bioacoustic encoder comparisons, training variants and representation analyses.

M1.justification: The default AG-CLIP architecture, checklist supervision and retrieval procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.18 adds an experimental variant with a 12-way month-prediction head and auxiliary cross-entropy loss, constituting a limited extension to the training objective.

E1.justification: v3 adds WABAD passive acoustic monitoring evaluation in A.9/Table A3. This substantially extends external testing to recordings collected under monitoring conditions, beyond iNatSounds focal recordings and curated XCDC dawn choruses. The original datasets and movie cases are retained.

E2.justification: Table A5 substantially expands the bioacoustic comparison set with BirdMAE, ProtoCLR and Perch 2.0, alongside frozen-MobileNet and Taxabind retrieval probes. These are actual evaluated alternatives, supplementing the unchanged original comparator sets. Table A10 also introduces a from-scratch comparator for species-identification transfer.

E3.justification: The original geolocation thresholds and core training settings are retained. Added protocols include frozen-encoder linear probes, ResNet50/ViT-B16 configurations, weighted training-data sampling, month-loss weight sweeps, top-1/top-5 species-identification transfer evaluation and entropy-ranked evaluation subsets. These substantially broaden the experimental design.

E4.justification: Appendices A.14–A.20 add taxonomic breakdowns, encoder and architecture ablations, geographic/species resampling tests, month-supervision sensitivity, representation analyses and checklist-uncertainty diagnostics. These investigate several previously untested failure mechanisms. The species-count distribution panel accompanying v2 Table 4 is removed, although its principal weekly-group observation remains in prose.

E5.justification: A.20/Figure A12 newly quantifies predictive uncertainty through normalized SINR-checklist entropy and reports error as uncertain recordings are excluded. Existing three-run mean/standard-deviation reporting and 100-run species-subset uncertainty bands remain unchanged; no increase in repeated-run counts is documented.

E6.justification: Scores in the retained Tables 1–4 and A1–A2 are unchanged. Substantial new results include WABAD AG-CLIP performance of 3439 km median error and 3.23% regional accuracy, a ResNet50 configuration reporting 935 km and 18.86%, and species-identification top-1 scores of 48.4% from scratch versus 50.7% after geolocation pretraining. These concern newly evaluated conditions.

T1.justification: A.20 introduces a quantitative definition of checklist uncertainty: entropy of predicted classwise probabilities normalized by the number of predicted positives. This extends the mathematical definitions used for analysis. The underlying geolocation formulation is retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, species-range, aggregation and multimodal contributions remain. v3 adopts a more explicitly bioacoustic framing and adds conclusion-level claims about transfer to real-world settings and audio geolocation being substantially harder than image geolocation.

C2.justification: The new Discussion develops explanations involving environmental sounds, broad species ranges and acoustic similarity across distant locations. Added appendices discuss resampling failures, limited month-supervision benefits, embedding confusions and confident prediction errors, while noting possible Perch training/evaluation overlap. The Impact Statement expands qualifications about geographic bias, evaluation overestimation and privacy.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents regression-coordinate normalization, existing dataset subsampling details and settings for added training variants. It replaces separate benchmark/code links with one project link and states an XCDC license. Availability statements are inconsistent: the introduction says models/code are available, whereas the Impact Statement promises release upon acceptance. Core hardware and training details are retained.

R1.justification: The benchmark-survey paragraph is replaced by a Species Identification subsection distinguishing geolocation from location-conditioned identification and auxiliary geolocation pretraining, including MetaPerch. References to newer bioacoustic encoders and passive monitoring are added. The principal positioning relative to image geolocation and soundscape mapping remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion undergo extensive revision. Problem setup and methodology are merged, regression/classification descriptions move to the appendix, and dedicated Discussion and Impact Statement sections are introduced. The appendix narrative is also substantially expanded and reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, Figure 1 moves above the abstract, and Figure 3's legend/colorbar arrangement changes. Table 4 is reordered and loses its species-diversity panel. New Tables A3–A10 and Figures A9–A12 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the benchmark's empirical credibility. WABAD tests passive-monitoring generalization, while Table A5 addresses v2's limited comparisons with specialist bioacoustic encoders. Added diagnostic and negative-result analyses clarify the method's applicability and weaknesses. These gains outweigh the removed diversity plot and inconsistent release statements, although some new causal interpretations remain speculative and reporting details for added experiments are limited.
